summary: Almost all of this mill's releases go straight into the Fox River, about 2 miles above where it meets the bay.

impacts.title: Fish & river life
impacts.how: About 230,000 lb of nitrates and 150 lb of ammonia reached the river in 2024. Extra nutrients feed algae that use up the oxygen fish need to breathe, and ammonia is directly toxic to fish at high levels. The mill also released 57 lb of lead, which settles into river mud and builds up in fish over time.

avoid.label: Check fish advice
avoid.text: Follow the Wisconsin DNR fish advisory for the Fox River before eating your catch

avoid.label: Keep smaller fish
avoid.text: Keep smaller, younger fish, and trim skin and fat, where pollutants collect

avoid.label: Less lawn fertilizer
avoid.text: Use less lawn fertilizer: runoff adds even more nutrients to the same river

impacts.title: Swimming & beaches
impacts.how: The Fox River carries these nutrients into the bay, where they can help fuel algae blooms that close beaches and turn the water green. The Fox is already listed as impaired for nutrients; this mill is one possible contributor.

avoid.label: Skip scummy water
avoid.text: Stay out of water that looks green, scummy or smells bad, and keep pets out too

avoid.label: Rinse off
avoid.text: Rinse off after swimming in the bay

impacts.title: Air in the neighborhood
impacts.how: About 14,700 lb of methanol and 3,900 lb of ammonia went into the air in 2024. Methanol can cause headaches and dizziness at high levels, and ammonia irritates the eyes, nose and throat.

avoid.label: Check air quality
avoid.text: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow) on hot, still days

avoid.label: Report odors
avoid.text: Report strong or unusual odors in the forum, where the company can reply. You can also call the DNR tip line, 1-800-847-9367

avoid.label: Close the windows
avoid.text: Keep windows closed when odors are noticeable

impacts.title: Birds & wildlife
impacts.where: Fox River and Green Bay shoreline
impacts.how: Lead and mercury don't break down. They build up in fish, then in the eagles, cormorants and gulls that eat them, and can harm their nerves and breeding.

avoid.label: Lead-free tackle
avoid.text: Use lead-free fishing tackle so less lead ends up in the river

avoid.label: Support restoration
avoid.text: Support shoreline habitat restoration along the lower Fox

avoid.label: Report sick birds
avoid.text: Report sick or dead birds near the mill in the forum, and let the Wisconsin DNR know too
